articles.title: Introducing the Overdrive Cup!
articles.summary: Last February, we launched the WASB Cups, a weekly tournament aimed at giving Overwatch teams of all skill levels the opportunity to train…
articles.body:
Last February, we launched the WASB Cups, a weekly tournament aimed at giving Overwatch teams of all skill levels the opportunity to train in official competitions. The goal was to improve their Elo and secure better seeding for OWCS and FACEIT League.

The WASB Cup allowed many teams to progress while also earning substantial rewards. Since its launch, the WASB Cup has seen:

More than 3,600 players participated in over 2,800 matches

$15,000 and over 18 million FACEIT Points distributed

In today’s blog, we will give you all the details about the Overdrive Cup , our brand new weekly tournament designed to help organized teams improve and sustain their careers.

The WASB Cups are gone, long live the Overdrive Cup!

Since their launch in February, we haven’t made any major changes to our weekly tournaments. With the Overdrive Cup , we wanted to revitalize the weekly cup concept, making it more appealing to players, while also helping teams of all skill levels improve throughout the week to enhance their performances in FACEIT League and OWCS.

This new initiative offers a fresh approach with attractive prizes and a live-streamed finals event, designed to give up-and-coming teams and grassroots players the opportunity to gain exposure within the community, as well as a new way to make their teams financially sustainable over time.

A free competition, using OWCS and FACEIT League rules, available in NA / EMEA / SA and OCE

Prizes that support teams in their ambition to become sustainable and break through in the competitive scene, with $2000 to be won each month and more than 2 million FACEIT points to be shared monthly

A multi-stage experience, featuring weekly tournaments leading up to the finals

Monthly Finals streamed by the community in multiple languages to provide greater visibility for teams and identify grassroots talent

Content creator teams will be invited to the Monthly Finals to boost the visibility of your team, but also to give you the chance to compete against big names in the community

Whether you are from NA , EMEA , SA or OCE , sign up now and experience our brand new Overdrive Cup! We hope this fresh format helps you refine your skills and strategies for FACEIT League and OWCS, while also setting you on the path to making your team sustainable, so you can launch into the high-level Overwatch scene.

As always, we’re excited to hear your feedback and answer any questions you may have, so don’t hesitate to join us on FACEIT Overwatch Discord .

As we continue to improve our competitions and the experiences we bring to Overwatch players on FACEIT, we’ll be back soon with announcements on exciting new features. In the meantime, we look forward to seeing many of you in the Overdrive Cup and wish you the best of luck in winning your matches!

articles.title: Two New NA Servers, Unlocking Nicknames, and Bringing a Touch of Anime to FACEIT in our October…
articles.summary: As we move into November, we’re back again with the last set of Patch Notes… for the FACEIT platform as you know it. Luckily, that’s the…
articles.body:
As we move into November, we’re back again with the last set of Patch Notes… for the FACEIT platform as you know it. Luckily, that’s the only spooky news we have for you this month, with positive changes to our NA server pool and tournament plugin to talk about instead! We’ve also included some long-awaited shop features, such as the anime collection out this month, and the ability to claim your nickname from an idle player coming soon! It’s been a pleasure to share how we’re improving FACEIT for you these past few months, and we’d love to know what you liked (or didn’t!) about our patch notes, so do let us know !

Play with better ping with new East and West Coast NA servers

We’re still working hard on connection issues based on your feedback , but we’re also picking up your feedback, and testing the impact of adding a wider variety of server locations! We’ve begun this effort by adding two new test server locations to NA matchmaking in San Jose and Virginia : aiming to provide better options for west and east coast players respectively looking for a server closer to home. To allow you to play in a more convenient location and test out the new servers, we’re still only requiring you to select 2 servers, out of a pool of 5 (previously 3). While this may increase queue times, we wanted to give you the flexibility to play with low ping should you choose, and the option to add other servers in the pool for shorter queue times remains available! As this is a test period, we’re especially eager to hear back from you about your experience, so let us know what you think!

Idle Nicknames soon purchasable in the FACEIT Shop!

The wait is nearly over! Soon, nicknames held by inactive accounts will finally be available for others to purchase. We understand how important your nickname is to you, so we’ve built in protections to prevent abuse or accidental loss. To begin with, a nickname will only be released after 12 months of account inactivity. Additionally, these inactive players will receive an email one week in advance, reminding them that logging into FACEIT resets the 12 month timer. To further protect this feature, nickname claiming is a FACEIT Premium perk, though free users can purchase it for $4.99 or 5000 FACEIT Points in the Shop. Premium users can claim a new username for free every three months. Plus, if your nickname is claimed, you’ll receive 1000 FACEIT Points — enough to choose a new one if you decide to return!

Level Up Your Style: Avatar Frames & Anime Collection available for purchase

You asked, we delivered! Avatar Frames are now live on FACEIT Shop, ready to be paired with your favorite Profile Cards or used solo to create striking, funky vibes. Choose between two designs — static (Circuit) and animated (Voltic) — both available in our debut FACEIT Collection in six vibrant colors. Just like Profile Cards, Avatar Frames show up not only on player profiles but also on play, matchroom, and league pages across FACEIT. Grab your favorites using FACEIT Points or your local currency.

That’s not all though! Recently, we introduced our latest release: the Anime Collection ! This limited-edition set features six unique Profile Cards and six epic Avatar Frames, each designed to bring a fresh, anime-inspired feel to your profile. Whether you’re into serene, dark, or explosive vibes, you’ll find the perfect combo to suit your style. Keep in mind that these are going fast, so don’t wait too long to secure your favorites.

Added !DHLDrops to FACEIT Watch streams… at the click of a button!

Released PoV sharing: you can now send your FACEIT Watch configuration for a stream or VOD with a shareable link!

Tidied up the layout of the homepage and VOD pages

Fixed a bug where 2 volume sliders would appear

The missions widget on the matchmaking screen can now display multiple missions

Added a player-sided round restore functionality — togglable by Organizers

Any team member can now select a side after winning a knife round if the team’s captain is not on the server instead of only the captain being able to select a side

Adjusted the automatic No-Show AFK forfeit logic to grant the win to the team with the most members present on the server

Moved the substitution phase to start after the map and server vetoes are finished. Previous: Match Scheduled -> Substitution (Lineup confirmation, if a team has substitutes) -> Server Veto -> Map Veto -> Match Ready New: Match Scheduled -> Server Veto -> Map Veto -> Substitution -> Match Ready

Added notifications for various Team roster management events

Added a two-step confirmation before banning a user from a League roster to prevent accidental removals

Added an option to view combined Standings from all of Leagues stage’s conferences

Added more detail to error messages when attempting to make roster changes

Added a “Go to Matchroom” button on the League overview page when the player is in a scheduled League match

The Player’s League division is now shown on their user profile under “Game Stats”

Updated the design of the Season Records panel on a user profile

When using “Find Team,” clicking on a team will now open an in-app modal instead of opening the team page in a new window

When using “Find Team,” Teams now have a “Copy Link” button above their Team roster panel

Team roster panel now has a “Make Officer” button visible for each player, only visible to the Team’s captain

Team Officers now have an icon in the Team roster panel

Bugfixes & Quality of Life improvements:

Added a notification when successfully updating rules on tournaments

The game registration panel now shows in a tournament header before joining

Middle-clicking on the “Team details” button on a roster modal now opens the team page in a new window instead of redirecting the user to it in the same tab

On Team pages, the Leagues participation history is now displayed in chronological order, sorted by most recent first

Tournament participants’ tabs now use infinite scroll pagination instead of a “Load more” button

Fixed a bug where registrations were not reopened after reopening signups on a tournament

Fixed a bug with Double elimination tournaments where it was not possible to disable double finals or change the number of slots

Fixed a bug where Swiss-system tournaments would get stuck generating rounds

Fixed a bug where it was not possible to disqualify a participant if the team had been already eliminated

Fixed a bug where copying a championship from the Organizer page would not work

Fixed a bug where teams were getting removed from tournaments after checking in

Fixed a bug where not-yet-started matches would show “STARTED NAN MINS AGO” on the Matches tab of Championships

Fixed a bug where some players in a Team roster would not appear on the “Manage Roster” panel

Fixed a bug where a league roster was available in the sidebar for players that were not part of the roster

articles.title: FACEIT Matchmaking Season 3 wraps up with yet another victory for donk!
articles.summary: It’s been another four thrilling months of Counter-Strike as amateur and pro players alike race for that coveted top spot on the FACEIT…
articles.body:
It’s been another four thrilling months of Counter-Strike as amateur and pro players alike race for that coveted top spot on the FACEIT Matchmaking leaderboards and their share of $100,000, as well as bragging rights and a stamp for up-and-coming players to show on their esports passport. Once again, donk has proven to be truly inevitable in his path to yet another victory, racking up a total of 5075 Elo — even more than he accrued last season!

The young prince of Counter-Strike hasn’t relented one bit this season, and racked up over 200 extra Elo this time round to firmly place himself at the very top once again! With a gap of 223 Elo over his next-closest contender and a third consecutive triumph over the rest of the world, what will it take to dethrone him? The task certainly isn’t easy: with a 69% win rate over 357 matches this season, bolstered by an impressive suite of stats, it would take an equally prodigal talent to even come close!

Want to know what it takes to play at donk ’s level, even against the best players in the world? We’ve got the recipe:

First, mix together the key ingredients to make sure your firepower is up to scratch:

Make sure to sprinkle in 10 knife kills and 1 Zeus for extra style, and maybe then you’ve got what it takes to challenge him!

While donk may have been too much to handle once again, the rest of the EU region has fought hard for their share of the prize money, with kyousuke from Spirit Academy and m0NESY from G2 rounding out the top 3 for a particularly young podium — the future of Counter-Strike looks scarier than ever!

NA After coming second last season, dea has claimed the top spot this time round, making a statement by blazing nearly 200 Elo ahead of Peeping and alter , who have both climbed 3 spots over their Season 2 placement — can one of them go all the way next time?

SA In South America, it’s pepe ’s turn to be crowned our champion, narrowly edging out Misfit to clinch the top spot and proving his worth as an up-and-coming talent, while clon7 closes out the podium. No other region has seen their leaderboard shaken up so much since last season: with only pepe and kye managing to keep their place among the top 10, who knows who the next champion may be?

On the other side of the world, our Asian leaderboard has been topped by Sange with 3978 Elo, followed by Anasasis and Crunchy

Meanwhile, the boys at SemperFi have locked up the entire Oceanic podium! shadiy leads the way with an impressive 4688 Elo, while his teammates keen and vision round up the top 3 in a true show of force for the team.

Over the next week, we’ll be handing out top 1000 badges to all winning players once correctly reassigned to the region they’ve played the most matches in this season — congratulations on your hard-earned prize!

That’s a wrap for FACEIT Matchmaking Season 3! We’re looking forward to Season 4, which is just around the corner with new heights to reach, fresh competition, a new Elo reset on season start and a couple surprises for you all coming later this month… Stay tuned to find out more!

articles.title: Community Showdown is back and it’s bigger than ever!
articles.summary: Community Showdown is back and bigger than ever!
articles.body:
Community Showdown is back and bigger than ever!

The first edition of the Community Showdown was a massive success, with over 20 tournament organizers bringing their communities together to claim a share of the $5,000 USD prize pool and more than 2 million FACEIT Points. Leading community names from around the globe joined the showdown, with over 400 teams participating, featuring teams from Ex Oblivione, Battletech, Grupo Senju, and many other communities, the tournament crowned Team Shikigami from the Overwatch Season community and Team Schweppes from the Hammerkick community as respective champions of the NA and EMEA regions.

Community Showdown is one of the largest Overwatch community competitions of 2024, and this second iteration promises to be even grander!

Benefit from the best Platform for your tournaments!

Staying true to our promise to the Overwatch community, we’re offering all select approved third-party tournament organizers free access to our platform’s infrastructure, enabling them to host and manage various tournament formats sustainably, easily, and efficiently. This allows organizers to engage their communities better than ever, while empowering Overwatch teams and players with consistent, rewarding, and aspirational content that extends beyond OWCS and FACEIT League events.

Selected third-party tournament organizers (you can apply here ) will automatically and freely receive:

A streamlined OW license request process, facilitated by FACEIT: FACEIT will now handle Blizzard license approvals on your behalf for hosting events on FACEIT. Simply apply through this link , and we’ll be in touch with you shortly with the outcome.

A seamless tournament experience for your tournaments: No more manual configurations! FACEIT allows you to smoothly manage every aspect of the match lifecycle (mode, map, side, and server selection) and report all results and stats back to the platform at the end of each match.

Easy onboarding with 24/7 support: Our experienced support team is here to guide you, ensuring you can offer the best competitive experience possible to your community.

More rewards for your community: Tournament organizers participating in Community Showdown II will offer 100,000 FACEIT Points as additional tournament prizing. FACEIT Points are our in-house currency, enabling your community to purchase Overwatch cosmetics, Overwatch Coins, and other products available in the FACEIT Shop .

Amplified communication for your events: To ensure the success of your events, you’ll benefit from exposure across FACEIT X , Instagram , TikTok , Organizer page , and Discord channels, maximizing your reach to attract even more players.

The opportunity to continue hosting your own tournaments after Community Showdown II: We’re thrilled to announce that select approved tournament organizers can keep using FACEIT’s integration with Overwatch, alongside our support, to run your own events for your community, providing them with the ultimate competitive experience.

Don’t wait — submit your application to host your tournaments here !

Introducing Community Showdown II with $7,500 and 3 Million FACEIT Points up for grabs

Starting 7th of December 2024, communities will compete across a variety of tournaments to secure a slot in the Community Showdown finals, taking place on 4th and 5th of January 2025. In total, $7,500 USD and over 3 million FACEIT Points are up for grabs for the participating teams. Here’s what to expect from Community Showdown II:

Selected third-party tournament organizers will host tournaments in their preferred format, qualifying their top teams for the $7,500 Community Showdown II finals.

100K FACEIT Points will be awarded to each organizer to support their tournament’s prize pool.

Each organizer will have the freedom to stream their competition, support co-streams, and create content on their channels without any restrictions.

Following our preliminary discussions with tournament organizers, we’re pleased to confirm the participation of the following communities.

Don’t miss out — join Community Showdown II by submitting your application here .

Join Community Showdown II, showcase your community, and host your tournaments on FACEIT!

We invite all community leaders eager to participate in Community Showdown II to apply now to host a tournament and benefit from the FACEIT platform and all of its advantages. Don’t miss this unique opportunity to bring your community consistent and recurring competitions throughout 2025 and beyond.

If you have any questions, feel free to reach out via email anytime at: organizers@faceit.com

Overwatch tournament organizers, we hope to see you soon on Community Showdown II!

articles.title: Climb to OWCS in FACEIT League Season 4 with multiple new improvements!
articles.summary: Don’t miss learning from the best Master teams as they battle for their share of $50,000 and glory with Season 3 playoffs this weekend…
articles.body:
Don’t miss learning from the best Master teams as they battle for their share of $50,000 and glory with Season 3 playoffs this weekend streamed here !

Gain more competitive experience as you enjoy new improvements for FACEIT League Season 4 including:

Start your climb to OWCS with FACEIT League

Earn your share of $800,000 with $200,000 just for tier-2 teams with 4 FACEIT League seasons in 2025

Find new friends who want to see how far they can go with our “ Find Team ” feature for Season 4

Helping fit League officials around your busy schedule with improvements including simultaneous offers, proposal history, and notifications when your opponents reply

Making our settings more Overwatch-specific by adjusting the veto and roster selection process

Understand League more easily with an updated season page

Learn more below about how your competitive Overwatch experience has been leveled up in Season 4!

If you missed the OWCS World Finals in Stockholm, here’s a quick recap. Other than wild strategies, world-class players, and passionate fans, we announced FACEIT League’s connection to OWCS ! Now, anyone can start their esports journey in the Open division and work their way to Overwatch’s most prestigious competition!

To help balance the divisions and make sure everyone starts competing at a level appropriate for their skill, there’s multiple free qualifiers at the start of next year so you can fast-track your competitive journey!

$200,000 for tier-2 teams with four seasons in 2025

We also announced a full year of competition for amateur teams competing for a minimum of $50,000 per season outside of OWCS. We guarantee four seasons of competition so teams have a consistent schedule of weekly official matches to look forward to. Instead of waiting months between qualifiers, teams can now work toward OWCS while still improving their skills.

This also includes prizes and competition for South America and Oceania where we hope to build the foundation in 2025 with active teams funding more opportunities for competitive players using the League Pass membership.

With FACEIT League registration closing in January, an incredible 350 teams have already started registering for Season 4 to see if they can climb to OWCS. With that, some teams don’t have a full team of 5 ready, just yet!

Don’t forget that you can use our “find team ” feature to browse teams who want to find players to gain competitive experience with! Join their teams and use the chat to coordinate when to play. You’ll get notifications in our FACEIT mobile app to easily stay on top of these for less time organising and more time practicing.

We are also aligning the FACEIT League roster size with OWCS so teams may have a maximum of 7 players and 1 coach. Keep in mind teams can still add up to 3 players per 7 days before the Roster Lock in case they need an emergency substitute.

Helping fit League officials around your packed schedule

It could be a real struggle to organise League matches around College, work, or other competitions. We’ve focussed on scheduling for Season 4 with multiple improvements to make it easier to find the time to join more competitive matches.

Avoid wasting time going back and forth with your opponents with times they won’t accept as we now highlight when you offer a proposal that was previously rejected. You can now offer multiple times simultaneously so your opponent can choose from several proposals at the same time. For example, if you can play multiple times on the same day or at the same time each night.

You can communicate faster with your opponents rather than writing in chat and hoping they notice the message as we’ve introduced “reasons” for rejecting an offer to communicate a specific response, eg “we can’t do Tuesday”. Finally, if your circumstances change, you can reject your own offer so you don’t need to worry if your opponents will accept the time.

It is now easier to stay on top of your League scheduling when away from your PC with notifications when offers are sent, accepted, or rejected. These notifications are sent using email, the bell at the top of the screen, and now the FACEIT mobile app .

During Season 3, we updated our process for both selecting rosters and how they would be displayed to make them more aligned with Overwatch.

For example, instead of players deciding who “starts”, at the beginning of each match teams will pick who is “red”. Similarly, instead of picking players before the map, at the start of a multiple-game series, teams will now pick their 5 players after the map has been selected. This way they can swap in any substitutes for that specific matchup.

As we continue to expand in Overwatch, more players who are less familiar with esports will be joining the platform. We have updated our season page so it is easier for you to understand how to join and start climbing to OWCS!

Good luck in Season 4 as you climb to OWCS through the skill-balanced division, gaining experience in weekly official matches, that are balanced around your schedule!

articles.title: Museum unveils newly restored Widow of Glencoe painting
articles.summary: Dundee-based conservators carried out work on the artwork, which was inspired by the Massacre of Glencoe.
articles.body:
A painting depicting the aftermath of the Massacre of Glencoe has been restored by Dundee-based conservators.

Almost 40 members of Clan MacDonald of Glencoe were killed in February 1692 after soldiers were ordered to attack them.

The painting, known as the Widow of Glencoe, shows a grieving woman standing next to the body of a man at the foot of a mountain with snow covering the ground.

Catriona Davidson, of Glencoe Folk Museum, said the "incredible" restoration of its painting had removed centuries of dirt - and revealed fine details, including a tear on the woman's cheek.

Generations of a family in Luxemburg had owned the 19th Century artwork before they donated it to Glencoe Folk Museum in 2023.

The painting is not signed and the only clue to who painted it is a motif called a monogram. Glencoe Folk Museum said it was believed the painter may have been an artist called James Goldingham.

There is a record of the artwork being exhibited at the Royal Academy of Arts in London in 1881.

Conservators Egan, Matthews & Rose completed the restoration as part of a major revamp of the museum.

Davidson told BBC Scotland News: "The detail they have pulled out of the painting is just incredible.

"The snow is a pure white it wasn't before. There is a tear on the woman's face that you couldn't really see before. It's an incredible transformation."

Groundworks begin on folk museum's £3m refurbishment

'Glencoe Massacre' coin hoard to be displayed in folk museum

A spokesperson added that further research would be done to confirm the artist.

Glencoe Folk Museum, which is housed inside two heather-thatched cottages in Lochaber, was set up more than 50 years ago by local women who stood in front of bulldozers to save the cottages from demolition.

It is home to 6,000 artefacts and its collection includes Jacobite relics and memorabilia from the two World Wars.

Work on a £3m revamp started last month and the new-look museum is set to open next spring.

An estimated 38 people were killed in the Massacre of Glencoe.

The MacDonalds were targeted because of their support for the exiled King James VII of Scotland, who was also James II of England before he was deposed in 1688.

The clan backed the restoration of the Stuart dynasty to the British throne and had taken part in the first Jacobite Rising of 1689.

Historians say they were late delivering an oath of allegiance to the Protestant King William III, and had been branded as rebels by the secretary of Scotland, Sir John Dalrymple.

articles.title: ‘Undoubtedly the GOAT’: Magnus Carlsen defends chess title at 2026 Esports World Cup
articles.summary: After winning the inaugural chess competition at the Esports World Cup last year, Magnus Carlsen successfully defended his crown after beating Denis Lazavik in straight sets in the Grand Final in Paris on Saturday.
articles.body: Magnus Carlsen has done it again. After winning the inaugural chess competition at the Esports World Cup (EWC) last year, the Norwegian Grandmaster successfully defended his crown after beating Denis Lazavik in straight sets in the Grand Final in Paris on Saturday. Incredibly, the world No. 1 went through the entire tournament without dropping a single game, finishing with 11 wins and nine draws as he took home the $250,000 first place prize and earned Team Liquid a crucial 1,000 Club Championship points – the American esports organization now sits 13th in the standings with 1,200 total points. The 35-year-old chess legend unsurprisingly entered the competition as the heavy favorite, as he’s spent a staggering 15 consecutive years as the world’s number one-ranked chess player – the longest such streak in modern International Chess Federation (FIDE) history. Despite this, Carlsen was nonchalant and said he wasn’t too concerned about the tournament when speaking to CNN Sports in Paris. “I don’t think too much about expecting to win,” Carlsen said. “You just want to do the right things and take it step by step… which is a very boring answer, but that’s a little bit how it is.” However, the Norwegian grandmaster did acknowledge he knows “it’s a likely scenario” for him to come out on top when he does enter competition. After all, he is also a five-time world classical chess champion and only relinquished his title after voluntarily deciding not to defend it in 2023, citing he was “not motivated to play.” But when the 35-year-old does have that fire in his belly, he’s almost unstoppable, and as Woman Grandmaster and chess influencer Nemo Zhou – who was also a commentator and analyst at the EWC in Paris – told CNN Sports without hesitation: “Magnus Carlsen is undoubtedly the GOAT. “Specifically mine, I would say yes – absolutely. There is nobody stronger in the history of the game.” Even with chess’ foray into esports, Carlsen’s dominance has not wavered as he is yet to lose a match at the EWC in his two title-winning campaigns, despite the format being vastly different to the classical form he first played when he reached the pinnacle of the game. The next moves for chess For some, it still may feel unnatural to see chess on a schedule alongside games like League of Legends, Tekken 8, Call of Duty Warzone and Fortnite at the EWC. After all, it’s an ancient game steeped in tradition with a history dating back centuries. But despite classical chess still being the most prominent form played on the global stage, shorter, online forms are now beginning to explode in popularity and it’s impossible to ignore. According to Chess.com – largely considered the home of online chess with over 250 million members – the 2025 EWC was the most-watched chess event of the year with just under 260,000 concurrent peak viewers, ahead of prestigious tournaments like Norway Chess and Tata Steel Chess. While the $1.5 million prize pool at last year’s EWC – which was the same figure for this edition – was the second-largest only behind the $2 million prize pool for the 2025 FIDE World Cup. However, the $2 million FIDE World Cup prize pool was split between 206 players, while just 16 players split the $1.5 million prize fund at last year’s EWC. “What’s happened here with the EWC the last couple of years is a really good step in the right direction,” Carlsen told CNN Sports, who also acknowledged that despite chess having “a lot of potential,” it does have “some limitations in terms of the ‘wow factor’ of the game.” To circumvent this, the EWC utilizes a “10+0” format, giving players just 10 minutes to make their moves without any chance of additional time, making games short, sharp, and more closely aligned with the other fast-paced esports games on show. It’s a new format for a new generation, but one which Carlsen still sets the standard for, making it no surprise the 35-year-old chess legend expressed he’s “really happy with the way things have gone the last few years.” He continued: “Chess is always going to be a game that a lot of people have some kind of relationship to. Even if they don’t play a lot, (don’t) know the rules, or just know some rules, everybody kind of knows something about chess. “We’re always going to have that advantage.” Next year, Carlsen will be going for his third-straight EWC title, and although he will likely have an even bigger target on his back, it would certainly not be wise to bet against him.

articles.title: Tropical Storm Moke set to impact storm-weary Hawaii
articles.summary: The storm could bring rounds of flooding rain to areas still recovering from Hurricane Lala.
articles.body: Hawaii is eyeing a new tropical threat less than a week after the deadly Hurricane Lala tore through parts of the islands. Tropical Storm Moke is swirling about 450 miles southeast of the eastern coast of the Big Island, according to the National Hurricane Center. Moke is forecast to maintain its intensity as a tropical storm and take a similar track as Lala toward Hawaii. But the new storm will be weaker than Lala and track farther south when it makes its closest pass on Sunday, somewhat dampening its wind threat, but not its rain. Lala’s eyewall brushed the southern coast of the Big Island while its center was roughly 30 miles offshore. The forecast brings this new storm’s center 200 miles south of the Big Island as a tropical storm. The exact distance could fluctuate in the coming days as the system becomes better organized. Weather forecast models are still trying to get a grip on the system’s strength, which is a key factor in its final track. A stronger storm would track farther north, closer to the islands, while a weaker one would stay farther offshore. Confidence in the storm’s track and intensity should improve soon. On Thursday, Hawaii’s Volcanoes National Park announced it will close at 5 p.m. Friday in advance of the storm. The park still doesn’t have power, internet or phone lines after Lala swept by last week, and many of its employees are still recovering from the storm, the announcement said. While this storm isn’t expected to come as close to the Big Island, its rainfall could be dangerous — and fall on the same places flooded last weekend. This means it will take far less rainfall to trigger “life-threatening flooding and mudslides,” the hurricane center warned. Five to 10 inches of rain are expected on the Big Island, with up to 15 inches possible on the central and eastern slopes. Confidence is lower for Maui and the other islands, but generally lower totals of 1 to 2 inches are expected, with isolated amounts up to 4 inches or more possible. Rainfall will begin on the Big Island by late Saturday night or early Sunday, local time, spreading to the other islands later Sunday night into Monday. Hawaii still reeling from Lala Hawaii is still deep in recovery after Lala dumped over 3 and a half feet of rain on the Big Island’s mountains, setting off devastating landslides and flash floods. A 93-year old woman died due to “storm-related injuries” on the Big Island last week, according to the Hawaii Police Department. Police are also investigating the death of an unidentified man in his 60s that they believe may have been storm-related. Mud, water, rock and debris destroyed large parts of Naʻalehu, in the southern part of the Big Island, smothering some houses in mud up to 10 feet deep, Hawaii Gov. Josh Green said in a news conference Thursday. Last week, Green said more than 100 homes were lost to Lala on the Big Island. Crews are still clearing downed trees and utility poles across the Big Island. Thousands are still without power, and roads washed away by floodwater are just starting to be rebuilt. Before the next storm hits, a team is also working to locate and secure human remains swept away from cemeteries inundated during the hurricane, Major Gen. Stephen Logan, adjutant general of the State of Hawaii Department of Defense, said in Thursday’s news conference. The team had recovered over 60 remains on Thursday, he said. The state is making plans to deal with more flooding, landslides and power outages by preparing supplies and hotel rooms for those who may be impacted by the storm, and monitoring water levels in the Wahiawa Dam, which rose more than 20 feet after Lala. Officials are urging residents in vulnerable areas to prepare now, as evacuation might be harder once the storm hits. “If you can leave a flood-prone area early, stay with friends or family, think about that now,” National Weather Service meteorologist John Bravender said. “So you can get ready for that before the rain starts this weekend.”

articles.title: Esports: How to get £2,000 to play computer games at university
articles.summary: Roehampton University offers students a year;y scholarship to play esports alongside their studies.
articles.body:
As parents across the country prepare to wave their children off to university, conversations about family finances and the cost of living are growing ever more frequent - and fervent.

Yet every year, millions of pounds worth of scholarships and bursary funding goes unclaimed by students - with many unaware the extra help exists.

So roll up the next generation of gamers, who this year can apply for as esports scholarship from the University of Roehampton - with more than 100 handed out so far.

But can the students balance their studies and their esports? And is the scholarship set to catch on?

Esports, meaning electronic sports, is the name for competitive video gaming.

It is different from standard video gaming as esports includes spectators, much like traditional sports.

Gamers compete against one another in high-stakes tournaments for cash prizes and trophies.

Roehampton is offering esports scholarships to undergraduate and postgraduate students who show that they can balance academic progress and video-gaming excellence.

"This scholarship is about recognising talent in a field that has a growing popularity both around the world and among our students," former University of Roehampton registrar Mark Ellul said.

Scholars are expected to compete in weekly university tournaments as well as representing the university at in-person events.

Roehampton requires minimum rankings in major games for the scholarship, but will consider applications from those close to the threshold who meet other criteria, such as having large followings on streaming platforms like Twitch.

Former esports scholar Cameron Dray found out about Roehampton through the esports scholarship. Inspired by similar initiatives at American universities, he looked into whether anything similar was on offer in the UK.

Initially, the university was offering just £1,500, but due to the team's performance and rise in popularity, the amount was raised to £2,000.

"This money was crucial to me as it gave me the opportunity to study in a very expensive city without the need for part-time work," Dray said.

"There were requirements that came alongside the scholarship, but none that were unexpected or not transparent when applying," he added.

Dray encouraged students to make use of every scholarship, bursary and opportunity available to them.

He said: "Many of these funds are available to more students than they realise, and everyone should be taking full advantage."

The average graduate in England leaves university with debts of more than £47,500 . Scholarships such as Roehampton's can reduce student debt and provide additional financial support.

Thomas Cole, an esports player nicknamed Pac who specialises in the racing game Trackmania, said universities offering unique scholarships, including esports, encourages students academically by reducing the level of financial stress they might face.

"Uni students being paid to play a game alongside doing their studies, it's definitely cracking. If I had gone to uni, I would have loved that," he says.

"If it doesn't let the academic side suffer, then I think being offered something like that really spurs on people to be better in gaming," he says.

Tom Allingham, student money expert from the Save the Student personal finance site, regularly advises incoming first years to seek out scholarships and learn more about what their university offers.

"Unfortunately, I don't think there is enough awareness on scholarships," he said.

"There is a lot of funding that goes unclaimed because students don't know that they're eligible for it," he added.

Save the Student helps share various scholarships and bursaries on their website.

"What we try to get across is you can get extra funding for so many different reasons."

articles.title: $7 million! AG.AL crowned Esports World Cup 2026 club champion after landmark Paris edition
articles.summary: Esports News: AG.AL were crowned Esports World Cup 2026 club champions after a dramatic final weekend in Paris, securing the $7 million (~INR 66.9 crore) top prize .
articles.body: AG.AL were crowned Esports World Cup 2026 club champions after a dramatic final weekend in Paris, securing the $7 million (~INR 66.9 crore) top prize following seven weeks of record-breaking esports action featuring more than 2,000 players, 200 Clubs and 25 tournaments across 24 games.AG.AL finished on 5,300 points, edging two-time defending champions Team Falcons, who ended runners-up with 4,600 points. Team Vitality finished third with 3,300 points, followed by Natus Vincere (2,950) and Team Liquid (2,700).The club championship went down to the wire, with AG.AL completing their campaign through Gwendal âGwenâ Duparc's victory in the inaugural Trackmania tournament. The Frenchman delivered under pressure to win the tournament and secure the club championship for AG.AL.Falcons had entered the Trackmania playoffs at the top of the overall standings, but Carl-Antoni âCarl Jr.â Cloutier's quarterfinal exit opened the door for AG.AL. Gwen then dominated the final, securing the $130,000 (~INR 1.2 crore) tournament prize and, more importantly, the club championship.AG.AL's title-winning campaign also featured a first-place finish in Tekken 8, second-place finishes in Chess, Free Fire and the Honor of Kings World Cup, and a third-place finish in Teamfight Tactics.AG.AL complete remarkable campaignâWhen we began expanding AG.AL globally in 2024, the same year the Esports World Cup launched, we set out to build a Club capable of succeeding across games, regions and cultures. This title shows how far that vision has come,â said Eddy Chen, COO at AG.AL.âOur journey in Paris reflected the strength of the entire organization, from M. Zubairâs breakthrough in TEKKEN 8 and our deep runs across multiple titles to Gwen delivering the decisive Trackmania victory under extraordinary pressure. But this trophy belongs equally to every player, coach and staff member whose dedication brought us here.âThe Paris edition also produced several memorable individual performances. France's Caliste âCalisteâ Henry-Hennebert led Karmine Corp to the League of Legends Grand Final in front of a home crowd, while 15-year-old Chilean Jaime âCraimeâ Bustos became the youngest Esports World Cup champion after defeating two EVO champions.AG.AL's Khawaja âM. Zubairâ also captured the Tekken 8 title, while Rocket League star Samy âdraliiâ Hajji became the first three-time Esports World Cup champion. Grandmaster Magnus Carlsen successfully defended his Chess title without losing a game.Paris delivers record numbersThe 2026 edition set new benchmarks for the Esports World Cup, with the event reaching 850 million viewers and generating 440 million hours watched â increases of 13% and 26%, respectively, year-on-year. Peak viewership reached 4.3 million during the League of Legends tournament.The event was distributed globally through more than 100 broadcast and OTT partners in 47 languages, with 5,000 creators and co-streamers supporting its coverage.In another major milestone, 175,000 tickets were sold for esports competitions, a 94% increase from 2025. Total visits across competition venues, Fan Fest and city activations exceeded two million during the seven-week event.âWe are proud of what the Esports World Cup has achieved in Paris and of its continued international growth,â said His Royal Highness Prince Faisal bin Bandar bin Sultan al Saud, Chairman of the Executive Committee of the Esports Foundation.âBringing the EWC to a global audience beyond Saudi Arabia marks an important milestone in its journey and reflects the growing recognition of esports as a global industry, connecting communities, cultures and audiences around the world.âParis was the first city outside Riyadh to host the Esports World Cup. More than 22,600 campaign placements across the capital reached 94% of Parisians, while the final weekend's Counter-Strike tournament was staged at the 20,000-seat Accor Arena.The event followed a year-long competitive journey involving more than 1.5 million players across 330 Road to EWC events.âOur ambition has always been bigger than a single event: to grow esports and establish it as a leading global sport,â said Ralf Reichert, Chief Executive Officer of the Esports Foundation.The Esports World Cup will return to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in 2027.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Man jailed for killing Leicester student over fake Rolex row
articles.summary: Harper Dennis was found guilty of manslaughter following a two-week trial at Leicester Crown Court.
articles.body:
A student who stabbed his former friend through the heart in Leicester after they fell out over a fake Rolex watch has been found guilty of manslaughter and jailed.

Harper Dennis, 19, plunged a knife five times into the chest of Khaleed Oladipo, 20, near De Montfort University in Leicester on the evening of February 3 this year.

A jury at Leicester Crown Court found Dennis not guilty of murder but guilty of manslaughter, having an offensive weapon and failing to provide the pin to his phone after a two-week trial on Tuesday.

Dennis, of Bath Lane, Leicester, was sentenced to a total of 10 years' imprisonment.

Prosecutor Jane Osborne KC told the jury Dennis killed Oladipo, who he made friends with through online gaming, because of a "perceived debt".

The trial heard their friendship soured after an unsuccessful attempt by Dennis to sell a fake Rolex given to him by Oladipo.

Judge Timothy Spencer KC told Dennis, who wore a dark suit in the dock, he had developed a "seething resentment" towards the victim.

He said: "You took a knife to the fight, you used it, this was not a one-off thrust of the knife but five separate applications and it should have been obvious to you this carried a high risk of serious harm."

He added: "The background is murky. You and Khaleed were certainly known to each other. You were probably, at times, pretty friendly.

"The moral high ground is simply not open to you. You have painted yourself as wronged, but the reality is the financial transactions in this case were all to do with scams.

"This money was designed to fund criminal activity. The dispute between the two of you was further fuelled by him providing a Rolex watch which you viewed as some part compensation for your losses, that turned out to be fake and that did not assuage your bitterness."

The judge said both Dennis and Oladipo had their "lives ahead of you".

He said: "This is not a case of a single desperate stab wound – this is one of five thrusts of the knife. You knew you had something serious in mind because you covered your face immediately before."

Oladipo's sister Precious Oladipo said in a victim impact statement that their mother had become withdrawn because she was "so unwell with grief".

She said: "The loss of a child is brain-altering. He was, in every sense, her light and joy and losing him has hollowed her out.

"She cries every single day, including at her workplace, the hospital. She mumbles that she sent Khaleed off to university, as she always did after the holidays, and he simply never came home."

She added: "The home we shared that was once full of laughter is now largely silent.

"Khaleed will not graduate, he will not see his 21st birthday, which he had been so looking forward to. Every future milestone will now be marked by his absence instead of his presence.

"We are bereft, there is no joy or happiness in our home. We move through life monotonously.

At about 17:00 GMT on the night he died, Oladipo left his girlfriend's flat carrying a plastic bag of leftover snacks and was on the phone to her while he walked back to his accommodation nearby to watch football.

But outside the De Montfort University's Innovation Centre, he was met by Dennis who was captured on CCTV walking up and down in the "busy" area.

"It took less than 30 seconds for the two men to come together, to struggle and for the defendant to leave," Osborne told the court.

The court was told Oladipo's girlfriend heard him say "why did you come up and stab me?" over the phone before asking for her to call the ambulance.

A post-mortem examination showed he had suffered six wounds, five to the chest including one which penetrated his heart, and one to his thumb.

Despite being taken to the Leicester Royal Infirmary, he was pronounced dead just over an hour after the stabbing, which took place near the DMU campus.

Giving evidence in his defence on Wednesday , Dennis said he was "fearful" for his life when Oladipo approached him with a knife, adding he was "wrestling" to prevent the 20-year-old from stabbing him.

In cross-examination, prosecutor Jane Osborne KC asked if Dennis knew he had stabbed Oladipo, to which he replied: "I didn't know and I didn't know he was hurt, and I didn't intend to cause any serious harm."

Jurors were shown CCTV footage of Oladipo and Dennis walking towards each other, with Osborne suggesting Dennis used his hands to open a folding knife.

Dennis denied the suggestion he had a knife in his possession, and said he did not leave his accommodation with one.

Addressing Dennis, the prosecutor said there was "bad feeling" between Dennis and Oladipo - and suggested Dennis left his accommodation with a knife "to settle it".

Dennis, who was a first-year business management student at the University of Leicester, told jurors he had been talking to Oladipo - who was in his third year at DMU - about money and "doing fraud".

He said: "Khaleed initiated it - saying that there are ways you can make money, and with these methods you will gain large amounts of profit through it, through these websites."

Dennis said he wanted to "make some profit", so sent Oladipo £6,000 - from his savings and money his parents had given him - but did not get his money back.

The defendant said Oladipo gave him a Rolex watch. Dennis added: "He said that the watch is real and you will be able to sell it and make the money back from it."

Dennis, the court heard, took the watch to a jewellers in Hatton Garden in Camden, London, and "was laughed at".

"Two jewellers looked at the watch, they examined it and realised it was fake," Dennis said.

"It made me feel a bit annoyed, bit kind of disappointed in Khaleed that he let me down."

Dennis, who told the court he had a gambling addiction, said he threatened to expose Oladipo online as someone who "can't be trusted" and a "bad businessman".

Det Insp Lorna Granville, from the East Midlands Special Operations Unit Major Crime Team, said: "It's a shocking set of circumstances and quite rightly, and expectedly, creates a huge impact on the student community.

"This is not deep entrenched criminality.

"What it appears is two young men with their lives ahead of them have had a falling out and one has reacted, I would say, completely disproportionately and unnecessarily to exact some retribution".

articles.title: El inesperado torneo que decide la cuarta plaza de Premier Padel
articles.standfirst: Yanguas y Nieto jugarán el FIP Gold de Belgrado, en el que también están inscritos Stupa y Sanz
articles.summary: Yanguas y Nieto jugarán el FIP Gold de Belgrado, en el que también están inscritos Stupa y Sanz
articles.body: Hace semanas se anunciaron las dos nuevas parejas que se formaban tras las rupturas del P1 de Londres. Mike Yanguas volvía a juntarse con Coki Nieto, mientras que Franco Stupaczuk pasaba a competir al lado de Jon Sanz. Todo apuntaba a que los españoles serían los que arrancarían como cuartos en el ranking por una distancia mínima, pero la cancelación del Major de Qatar ha provocado que se cambien los papeles, obligando a estas dos duplas a pelear por ese privilegiado puesto en el FIP Gold de Belgrado que se celebra esta semana. Cuando se unieron, Yanguas y Coki figuraban como cuartos en la lista de inscripciones del P1 de Madrid, superando por tan solo 21 puntos a Jon y Stupa. Esa posición permite evitar a los principales candidatos al título hasta semifinales, dejando un camino mucho más asequible sobre el papel. Una ventaja que el motrileño y el madrileño esperaban mantener, pero que se ha visto alterada por un condicionante inesperado. Premier Padel suspendió la prueba prevista en Doha en el mes de abril. Se trata de la cita que más puntos reparte, la cual fue sustituida por Kuwait, torneo que tendrá lugar en noviembre. Sin embargo, existía un problema con los puntos de 2025, que debían restarse precisamente con la disputa del Major de Qatar. Al no haberse celebrado, la organización optó por restar de manera progresiva el resultado conseguido la pasada temporada. Por tanto, aunque no haya torneo en juego, los jugadores continúan perdiendo esas unidades semana a semana. Mike y Nieto alcanzaron las semifinales en la edición anterior, mientras que Jon solo llegó a cuartos. Stupa, por su parte, no pudo ni siquiera participar por problemas físicos. Esta circunstancia ha provocado que los primeros hayan descontado más puntos desde su unión tras el P1 de Londres hasta la fecha, dejando a Franco y Sanz en la cuarta plaza por 55 unidades; una situación que ni siquiera los propios protagonistas conocían de antemano. “Mi objetivo con Franco era recuperar la cuarta plaza. Él me llamó pensando que íbamos a ser quintos y hace un par de días me enteré de que seríamos cuartos en Madrid”, explicó el drive navarro en Padel Addict. Con la pugna en un margen tan estrecho, ambas parejas se han inscrito en el FIP Gold de Belgrado. Se trata de una prueba de la quinta categoría del circuito internacional (por debajo de Major, P1, P2 y FIP Platinum) que otorga 150 puntos a los ganadores. Un botín que supondría un intercambio de posiciones de cara al Major de París, dado que el P1 de Madrid ya cerró sus inscripciones con Jon y Stupa como cuartos cabezas de serie. Así pues, lo que ocurra en tierras serbias determinará quién llega con ventaja a Roland Garros. Ambas duplas parten como las principales candidatas al título, ostentando la condición de cabezas de serie uno y dos de la cita. También figuraban inscritos Aimar Goñi y Edu Alonso, aunque finalmente no acudirán. Por el lado de Yanguas y Coki, Álex Ruiz y Javi García se perfilan como la mayor amenaza, mientras que Jon y Stupa se cruzarían en su camino con duplas como Jofre-Bautista o Xisco Gil-Pablo Lijó. En cualquier caso, todo apunta a un hipotético cruce en la final para definir la cuarta plaza en París. No obstante, si Sanz y Stupaczuk no alcanzan la ronda definitiva, les valdría con que Mike y Nieto no levanten el título para mantener su posición. Una batalla que se librará semana a semana y que marcará el arranque de estos dos nuevos proyectos en la élite.

articles.title: Major gangland figure Steven Daniel arrested in organised crime raid
articles.summary: Steven 'Bonzo' Daniel was arrested on Wednesday at his home in the north of Glasgow.
articles.body:
One of Scotland's most high-profile gangland figures has been arrested during an early morning police raid.

Steven 'Bonzo' Daniel, 46 was taken into custody at around 06:00 from his home in Robroyston in the north of Glasgow.

Daniel is understood to be the head of the notorious Daniel crime family which has been engaged in a violent feud with the rival Lyons family for 25 years.

He was arrested in connection with serious and organised crime, firearms and drugs offences as part of Operation Ventetic, a major UK-wide operation which has dismantled several gangs.

BBC Scotland News joined the operation shortly before sunrise.

Dozens of officers involved were briefed at a nearby police station before joining a convoy to Daniel's home.

Two uniformed officers initially approached the property and spoke to him through a first-floor window.

An officer with a police dog then moved in.

Moments later Daniel left the property through the front door and was taken into the back of a police van.

A second man, Steven Gordon, 39 was also arrested in Garthamlock, less than four miles away, in a simultaneous operation.

He was taken into custody in connection with serious and organised crime, firearms and drugs offences and conspiracy to murder.

Assistant Chief Constable Dave Ferry said: "The chief constable has made it clear that those intent on being involved in serious and organised crime will be brought to justice.

"This enforcement action underlines that commitment.

"We will continue to take strong action and to use every tool and tactic available to relentlessly pursue those involved in serious criminality who seek to profit from the harm and misery they cause to communities in Scotland."

The Scottish arm of Operation Venetic has resulted in more than 60 arrests since 2020 when the National Crime Agency penetrated a secret communications system used by criminals.

In May 2017 Daniel suffered serious facial wounds when he was attacked after a 100mph car chase through Glasgow.

articles.title: 'No major damage' for Forfar player after game abandoned for neck injury
articles.summary: Forfar Athletic say Adam Livingstone has not suffered any major damage after Tuesday's Challenge Cup match against Formartine United was abandoned because of...
articles.body:
Forfar Athletic say Adam Livingstone has not suffered any major damage after Tuesday's Challenge Cup match against Formartine United was abandoned because of a neck injury suffered by the defender.

Forfar led 1-0 when Livingstone was hurt in an aerial clash early in the second half.

He received treatment on the pitch and was subsequently taken to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee, where he stayed overnight.

"Following last night's injury, Adam was taken to Ninewells Hospital where X-ray results have not shown any major damage," Forfar said in a statement on Wednesday.

"Adam was kept in hospital overnight but we have been advised that, all being well, he should be allowed home later today."
